so demonstrating 90 percent reliability at 95 percent confidence needs

$$n = \frac{\ln 0.05}{\ln 0.90} = 28.4, \ \text{so 29 consecutive successes}$$

against a programme total of thirty-one vehicles. **The X-9 could not have demonstrated its own reliability to any useful confidence even if every flight had succeeded**, which is a general property of small flight-test programmes and not a criticism of this one.

## Comparison With Ground Prediction

The comparison available here is unusually good, because the configuration family the X-9 belonged to was measured independently and at length by the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics, abbreviated NACA, using the rocket-model technique described in the earlier articles of this series.

[Moul and Wineman 1952][research_moul_1952], [Baber and Moul 1955][research_baber_1955], and [Brown 1957][research_brown_1957] each flew instrumented cruciform canard missile models across the transonic and low supersonic range, and [Niewald and Moul 1950][research_niewald_1950] measured control effectiveness and hinge moments for the same class. [Spearman 1961][research_spearman_1961] gives tunnel results for a series of cruciform-wing missiles with canard controls at Mach 2.01, and [Peterson 1961][research_peterson_1961] covers static stability and control of canard configurations from Mach 0.7 to 2.22. The tunnels themselves were being extended to the relevant conditions in the same years, and the instrumentation and technique reports of [Diggins 1951][research_diggins_1951], [Smith 1953][research_smith_1953], and [Adams and Rubin 1958][research_adams_1958] are the reason those measurements exist. The bomber the X-9 was to be carried by had its own tunnel programme, reported by [Shantz 1953][research_shantz_1953] and [Anderson 1958][research_anderson_1958].

**This is a denser independent measurement base than any previous vehicle in this series enjoyed**, and the cause is structural, not fortunate. A canard cruciform missile is a configuration family rather than a single aircraft, many organisations wanted the same derivatives, and the rocket-model technique could produce them quickly. The X-1's transonic drag rise had to be measured by the X-1 because nothing else was shaped like an X-1.

The prediction problem is correspondingly easier and the article should say so. What the X-9 had to determine for itself was not the aerodynamics but the closed-loop behaviour, and no wind tunnel produces a miss distance.

The one place where prediction was hard is the interaction between the guidance loop and the airframe under realistic noise, and the analytical apparatus for that arrived after the X-9 finished flying. [Abramovitz 1952][research_abramovitz_1952] and [Abramovitz 1953][research_abramovitz_1953] treat the speed of response of proportional navigation systems and the effect of missile configuration on it, [Stewart and Smith 1959][research_stewart_1959] synthesise optimum homing guidance with statistical inputs, and [Stewart 1961][research_stewart_1961] gives an explicit linear filtering solution for the same problem. **The two Stewart reports postdate the X-9's last flight and the two Abramovitz reports appeared as it was ending**, and the X-9's guidance was designed and flown without them. The line continues through the three-dimensional formulation of [Adler 1956][research_adler_1956], the final-value formulation of [Abzug 1967][research_abzug_1967], the closed-form solution of [Guelman 1974][research_guelman_1974], and the comparative evaluation of [Price and Warren 1973][research_price_1973]. [Potter 1964][research_potter_1964] separates guidance from navigation, which makes any of it tractable, and [Aldrich and Krabill 1972][research_aldrich_1972] supply the state estimation that modern guidance assumes.

**A programme that finished in January 1953 was using none of this**, and the gap between what the X-9 flew and what the theory would later say it should have flown is a fair measure of how far ahead of its analysis the practice ran.

## What the Data Changed

### The RASCAL and Its Cancellation

The X-9's direct consequence is the GAM-63. The operational missile used the X-9's canard configuration and a rocket engine derived from the X-9's, in a body nine feet longer and two feet larger in diameter. The programme was cancelled in September 1958 \[[GAM-63 RASCAL][ref_rascal]\].

**A testbed whose weapon is cancelled has an ambiguous legacy, and an honest account has to say so.** The X-9 met its objectives. The weapon it served never became fully operational. The cancellation is attributed to the weapon's limited range and accuracy and its toxic liquid propellants \[[Parsch 2002][ref_parsch_x9]\], to the Strategic Air Command's judgement that it was already obsolete, and to a 1958 test record in which one of 65 scheduled launches succeeded \[[GAM-63 RASCAL][ref_rascal]\], none of which are failures of the X-9. The [standoff weapon][ref_standoff] role passed to the [AGM-28 Hound Dog][ref_hound_dog] and later to [air-launched ballistic missiles][ref_alcm] such as Skybolt, both of which [Jenkins Landis and Miller 2003 American X-Vehicles, An Inventory X-1 to X-50][book_jenkins_landis_miller_2003] names among the later standoff weapons for which the X-9 served as a conceptual prototype, and [Werrell 1985 The Evolution of the Cruise Missile][book_werrell_1985] traces the wider evolution of the category.

### The Error Budget as a Method

The method survived, and the hardware did not.

Specifying a weapon by a circular error probable, decomposing that figure into an error budget allocated across subsystems, and verifying it statistically over a flight programme is now how guided weapons are procured. The statistical machinery was still being worked out while the X-9 flew, in [Moranda 1959][research_moranda_1959], [Moranda 1960][research_moranda_1960], and [Kamat 1962][research_kamat_1962], and the connection between accuracy and effect through a damage function was made explicit by [Lilliefors 1957][research_lilliefors_1957].

The argument as a whole leads to this relation, so it is set out in full. For a weapon with a lethal radius $R_L$ against a given target, delivered with circular error probable $\mathrm{CEP}$, the single-shot kill probability is

$$P_k = 1 - \left( \tfrac{1}{2} \right)^{\left( R_L / \mathrm{CEP} \right)^{2}}$$

which equals one half when the lethal radius equals the circular error probable, and rises steeply thereafter. The relation assumes a definite lethal radius, and neither the lethality nor the aim point is that clean in practice. [McNolty 1965][research_mcnolty_1965] treats the case where the lethal effect is itself a random variable, [Braithwaite 1962][research_braithwaite_1962] the extrapolation of sparse kill-probability data, and [Lilliefors 1957][research_lilliefors_1957] gives the hand computation the period used. **The shape of the damage function turns out to matter more than the accuracy fed into it**, as [Moon 2021][research_moon_2021] finds, and the structural-response side that determines that shape is now simulated in [Temsah et al. 2021][research_temsah_2021] and predicted by learned models in [Almustafa and Nehdi 2020][research_almustafa_2020]. Inverting for the accuracy required to reach a given kill probability,

$$\mathrm{CEP} = \frac{R_L}{\sqrt{\log_2 \left( \dfrac{1}{1 - P_k} \right)}}$$

The weapon-effects relations behind the lethal radius are [Glasstone and Dolan 1977 The Effects of Nuclear Weapons][book_glasstone_dolan_1977], with [nuclear weapon yield][ref_nuclear_yield] scaling and [terminal ballistics][ref_terminal_ballistics] setting the conventional case. **And here the programme's founding irony becomes arithmetic.** The lethal radius is not free either, and it scales with yield in a way that makes the accuracy requirement collapse. Blast effects scale with the cube root of yield, so the radius at which a given overpressure is reached is

$$R_L = R_1 \, W^{1/3}$$

with $W$ the yield in kilotonnes and $R_1$ the one-kilotonne radius, which for the five pounds per square inch contour that destroys ordinary structures is about 0.43 miles, or 690 metres, for an air burst \[[Glasstone 1962 The Effects of Nuclear Weapons, Revised Edition][book_glasstone_1962]\]. A twenty kilotonne weapon therefore gives

$$R_L = 690 \, (20)^{1/3} = 1873 \, \text{m}$$

and a larger warhead gives 3,200 metres at 100 kilotonnes and 6,900 metres at a megatonne. **Every factor of eight in yield doubles the tolerable circular error**, and this arithmetic underlies the observation that accuracy and yield are substitutes. [Morton 1966][research_morton_1966] covers the scaling and the target-dependence that make the choice of overpressure contour a judgement rather than a constant, with the vulnerability of a specific class of target in [Andon 1965][research_andon_1965]. For a warhead with a lethal radius of 1,500 metres against a soft target, corresponding to something near ten kilotonnes on this scaling, the accuracy needed for a 90 percent kill probability is

$$\mathrm{CEP} = \frac{1500}{\sqrt{\log_2 10}} = \frac{1500}{1.82} = 823 \, \text{m}$$

against the 108 metres the 1945 specification demanded. **The requirement that dimensioned this vehicle was about eight times tighter than the weapon it carried needed.** It was written one day before Trinity, and the MX-767 project it produced was already to develop a nuclear-armed missile \[[GAM-63 RASCAL][ref_rascal]\], so the warhead changed almost at once and the accuracy figure in the record remains the 1945 one.

This does not make the X-9 pointless. It relocates its value. The accuracy work was largely surplus to the nuclear mission and directly applicable to everything that came after it, and the reliability, the launch procedures, and the trained crews were not surplus at all.

### The Configuration

The cruciform canard layout the X-9 flew became common, and the measurement base assembled around it in the early 1950s outlived both the X-9 and the RASCAL. The reports cited in the Comparison section above were still being used as design data long after the vehicles that motivated them were scrapped, and the measurement programme continued past the X-9's end in [Bright and Peterson 1960][research_bright_1960], [Foster 1959a][research_foster_1959], [Anderson 1961][research_anderson_1961], and [Robinson 1958][research_robinson_1958], with the hinge-moment case extended to rolling and manoeuvring flight by [Pfenneberger 1966][research_pfenneberger_1966] and the prediction technique itself criticised by [Abel 1971][research_abel_1971].

**A configuration family outlives the programmes that motivate it**, and the family is a more durable contribution than the vehicle. The consolidated design data of the period, in [Army War Coll Carlisle Barracks Pa 1952][research_army_war_coll_carlisle_barracks_pa_1952] and its later volume [Advanced Fuel Research INC East Hartford CT 1957][research_advanced_fuel_research_inc_east_hartford_ct_1957], is where such measurements ended up.

### Optimal Guidance Laws

The guidance problem the X-9 solved by putting a man in the loop is now solved by an optimisation. Modern treatments derive the guidance law from a cost functional rather than from a geometric rule, and the [proportional navigation][ref_pronav] the period was working out is recovered as a special case, a connection made explicit by [Lee and Cho 2021][research_lee_2021], who show pure proportional navigation to be inverse-optimal for a particular cost, and by [Jeon et al. 2020][research_jeon_2020]. [Weiss and Shima 2019][research_weiss_2019] and [Weiss and Shima 2021][research_weiss_2021] give the linear quadratic formulation and [Lin and Xin 2019][research_lin_2019] the state-dependent Riccati approach. The impact-angle and impact-time constraints that a modern weapon carries and the X-9 did not appear in [Jung and Lee 2024][research_jung_2024] and [Erer et al. 2024][research_erer_2024], the biased form that a landing or a glide requires in [Yang 2025][research_yang_2025] and [Levin and DeLaurentis 2025][research_levin_2025], and the emulation of an optimal law by a virtual target in [Merkulov et al. 2025][research_merkulov_2025]. Disturbance attenuation with measurement feedback is treated by [Or et al. 2021][research_or_2021], and the multi-agent extension the period could not have imagined by [Shalumov 2019][research_shalumov_2019]. Closed-form solutions of the linearised equations, the analysis [Abramovitz 1952][research_abramovitz_1952] was attempting with the tools of 1952, are now available in [Markham 2019][research_markham_2019] and [Markham 2024][research_markham_2024]. [Bryson and Ho 1975 Applied Optimal Control][book_bryson_ho_1975] supplies the theoretical frame for all of it.

[Weiss and Shima 2021][research_weiss_2021] also give the minimum-effort formulations that bound how little control authority an intercept needs, and [Bhattacharjee et al. 2021][research_bhattacharjee_2021] the model-predictive treatment that carries explicit constraints.

**What has not changed is the error gradient argument.** A guidance law of any sophistication still cannot beat the geometry of where its sensor sits. Terminal seekers exist because of that geometry, and so does the modern equivalent of the RASCAL link, a synthetic-aperture radar image formed by the weapon itself, as [Sun et al. 2024][research_sun_2024] describe.

### Robust Autopilots

The inner loop the X-9 needed to hold its fast airframe while the operator flew slowly is now designed against explicit uncertainty rather than against a nominal model. [Simões and Cavalcanti 2023][research_simoes_2023] use a structured linear parameter-varying formulation, [Sun et al. 2023][research_sun_2023] a gain-scheduled multifidelity design, [Zhou et al. 2023c][research_zhou_2023] dynamic surface control, [Lee et al. 2020][research_lee_2020] robust backstepping with an explicit time-delay term, and [Gao et al. 2021][research_gao_2022] a differential-game formulation. The actuator that closes the loop has its own literature, since an electromechanical surface actuator is now the default, and [Maré 2022][research_mare_2022] and [Ruan et al. 2021][research_ruan_2021] treat its sizing and its friction, with fault identification in [Quattrocchi et al. 2022][research_quattrocchi_2022] and fault-tolerant reconfiguration in [Li et al. 2026a][research_li_2026_2]. **A hydraulic actuator of the X-9's period could fail in one way and a modern electromechanical one can fail in several**, so the literature is about diagnosis, not power. The flutter boundary that an all-moving surface brings is now computed and actively suppressed in [Li et al. 2023d][research_li_2023_4].

### Data Links and the Latency Problem

The X-9's loop closed across a radio path short enough that its delay was negligible, and the operator was the slow element. The modern version has the delay in the network rather than in the human, and closing a loop across a variable delay is a separate subject. [Ma and McDonald 2026][research_ma_2026] identify the latency thresholds at which a human operator's performance breaks down, the direct descendant of the crossover argument above. Compensation schemes are [Chen and Liu 2021][research_chen_2021] using a Smith predictor, [Shen et al. 2019][research_shen_2019] and [Dehghan et al. 2021][research_dehghan_2021] for the bilateral case, and [Kim et al. 2024][research_kim_2024_2] for outlier detection in the delay itself. [Florencio et al. 2020][research_florencio_2020] cast it as a networked-control problem.

### Computed Canard Aerodynamics

The derivatives the rocket-model programme measured are now computed, and the configuration continues in service. [Zhao et al. 2025c][research_zhao_2025] give a nonlinear body-aerodynamic model for a canard-controlled round, and [Tai et al. 2023a][research_tai_2023] and [Tai et al. 2023b][research_tai_2023_2] identify parameters from flight, the task the rocket-model technique performed by other means. Configuration studies of the kind that filled the 1950s reports continue in [Shumway and Boranian 2025][research_shumway_2025], with the tunnel-and-simulation parameter estimation that succeeded the rocket-model technique in [Singh and Ghosh 2023][research_singh_2023], and **the modern question is not what the derivatives are but how much a wrong derivative costs**, which [Li et al. 2025f][research_li_2025_4] answer by propagating aerodynamic modelling error into the closed-loop dynamics. The X-9's designers could not ask that question, because they had no closed-loop model to propagate the error through.

### Store Separation

The problem the trapeze solved by avoidance is now solved by computation and by scaled free-flight testing. [Song and Ai 2021][research_song_2021_2] analyse aircraft and store compatibility for an internal weapons bay, the same geometry as the X-9's, and the similarity laws that make a tunnel test meaningful are derived by [Xue et al. 2019b][research_xue_2019], [Xue et al. 2020b][research_xue_2020], and [Xue et al. 2020a][research_xue_2020_2]. Air launch persists as a category, and [Stewart et al. 2026][research_stewart_2026] treat the flight dynamics of a modern air-launched vehicle, with the design optimisation in [Li et al. 2022e][research_li_2022_6] and the smallest end of the category in [Elliott et al. 2025][research_elliott_2025].

### Where the Mission Went

The standoff strike role the RASCAL was built for did not disappear, it accelerated. Boost-glide vehicles now occupy the niche, and the guidance and control problems are recognisably the same ones scaled up, with [Bao et al. 2021][research_bao_2021] integrating guidance, control, and morphing, [Autenrieb and Gruhn 2026][research_autenrieb_2026] allocating control across redundant surfaces, and [Jiang et al. 2022a][research_jiang_2022] treating the interception problem from the weapon's side. [Chen et al. 2024][research_chen_2024] and [Zang et al. 2025][research_zang_2025] take the defensive side. **The X-9's descendants are being shot at by systems the X-9's designers assumed would not exist**, and [Wang et al. 2024a][research_wang_2024] develop counter-guidance that treats proportional navigation as something to be defeated rather than used. Trajectory optimisation is studied for the cruise case by [Shachar et al. 2025][research_shachar_2025] and for the ascent case by [Lei et al. 2025b][research_lei_2025], and [Cheah et al. 2025][research_cheah_2025] and [Gao et al. 2026b][research_gao_2026] address the flight-test control synthesis that such a vehicle now needs.

The other direction the mission went is multiplication. Where the X-9 carried one operator's attention to one target, air-launched effects now go in numbers and coordinate among themselves, which changes the accuracy requirement rather than tightening it, and [Burchett 2019][research_burchett_2019] studies the cooperative localisation that makes it work. **A weapon that can be produced in quantity substitutes redundancy for precision**. The yield scaling above describes the same substitution, bought a different way.

### Test Instrumentation

The measurement problem has moved from getting data down to knowing whether to believe it. [Ryu et al. 2022][research_ryu_2022] predict sensor data in missile flight tests to detect faults, [Fontana and Di Lauro 2022][research_fontana_2022] survey the sensors themselves, and [Głębocki and Jacewicz 2020][research_g_ebocki_2020] combine sensitivity analysis with flight results in the way a modern version of this programme would.

### Estimating the Circular Error

The statistical question the X-9 programme faced, how to estimate a percentile of a two-dimensional distribution from a few dozen samples, has not gone away, and **the surprising thing is how little the answer has changed**. The estimators compared by [Moranda 1959][research_moranda_1959] and [Kamat 1962][research_kamat_1962] and the bias treatment of [Moranda 1960][research_moranda_1960] are still the estimators, and the modern literature on weapon accuracy is largely about getting more samples rather than about extracting more from few. Where the effort has gone is into predicting the trajectory well enough that the sample is not needed, as [Zang et al. 2025][research_zang_2025] and [Chen et al. 2024][research_chen_2024] show for the interception problem.

**A programme that flies twenty-two times still cannot measure its own seventy-fifth percentile**, and no amount of estimator sophistication repairs that.

### Proportional navigation, the miss distance and modern guidance laws

**The guidance law and what it leaves at the target.** Proportional navigation and its variants, the miss distance and its adjoint analysis, optimal, differential-game and sliding-mode laws, and integrated guidance and control. **The constrained impact belongs to this century.** 280 of these titles name an impact angle or an impact time, the earliest dated one is from 2003, and 270 of the 278 dated ones are from 2010 or later, which agrees with the review above, where impact-angle and impact-time constraints are what a modern weapon carries and the X-9 did not.

### Rocket propulsion, throttling and combustion stability

**The propulsion the two chambers stand for.** Liquid and solid rocket engines and motors, injectors and feed systems, regenerative and film cooling, throttling, and thrust chamber life. **205 of these titles name combustion instability or combustion stability**, 60 of them dated before 1970, against 37 that name throttling. Solid propellant motors, which this vehicle did not use, account for 79 titles and are kept as part of the same combustion literature.

**The tracker and the errors the beamwidth calculation leaves out.** Monopulse and conical-scan angle measurement, glint and scintillation, low-angle tracking and multipath, seekers, the jamming of trackers, and the filters that turn measurements into tracks. 164 of these titles name monopulse. **Glint is not a closed subject.** 85 titles name it, and 40 of the 74 dated ones are from 2010 or later, which agrees with the statement above that glint remains a live subject.

### Missile airframe aerodynamics, canard and cruciform

**The canard cruciform family and the missile airframe at large.** Canard and tail control, cruciform wings and fins, induced roll and roll control, hinge moments, slender-body theory and the prediction of supersonic missile aerodynamics. **The cruciform is a period word.** 53 titles name it, with a median year of 1973, and one is dated 2010 or later, while the canard continues in 175 titles, 35 of them from 2010 or later.

### Autopilots, actuators and inertial instruments

**The inner loop and the instruments that feed it.** Missile autopilot design by every method from classical loop shaping to sliding modes and linear parameter-varying synthesis, fin actuators, gyroscopes and their drift, inertial navigation and alignment, and the structural coupling of a flexible airframe. 289 of these titles name an autopilot. 87 name a gyroscope, 61 of the 84 dated ones are from 2010 or later, and 40 name a micro-machined, fibre-optic or resonator device, which is the inexpensive instrument The Autopilot Inner Loop credits with inverting the architecture.

### The human operator and control across a delay

**The man who closed the loop, and the loop he became.** Manual control and its models, the crossover model, compensatory and pursuit tracking, operator workload and situation awareness, the allocation of functions between the operator and the automation, and teleoperation across a communication delay. **The subject moved from the operator to the delay.** The 92 titles that name manual control, manual tracking or compensatory tracking have a median year of 1983, and the 179 that name teleoperation have a median year of 2016.

### Command, beam-rider and homing architectures

**Where the sensor sits.** Command to line of sight, beam riding, semi-active and active homing, television and optical command guidance, midcourse guidance and the strapdown seeker. **The beam rider is a period architecture.** 15 titles name it, with a median year of 1963, while 104 name homing.

## Where the Framing Breaks Down

Treating the X-9 through an error budget is productive and it misleads in several ways.

**The X-9 is not an X-plane in the sense the series began with.** It is a subscale development article for a weapon, designated retrospectively in 1951 \[[Parsch 2002][ref_parsch_x9]\], and the designation carries no research content that the RTV-A-4 label did not.

**The accuracy framing overstates what the vehicle was for.** The programme's stated objectives included checkout and launch procedures, crew training, and deployment experience, none of which reduce to a variance, and the programme's history lists them among its purposes \[[GAM-63 RASCAL][ref_rascal]\].

**A testbed cannot be evaluated independently of its weapon.** The X-9 succeeded and the RASCAL was cancelled \[[GAM-63 RASCAL][ref_rascal]\], and any account that treats the first fact without the second is telling half of it.

**The two-architecture argument is cleaner in retrospect than it was at the time.** This article derives the launcher-guided range limit from a beamwidth and asserts that it explains the programme's shape. The record does not show anyone making that calculation, and the inference is the author's.

## The Source Base

**The survey rests on 6,105 research records assembled from Crossref, the NASA Technical Reports Server and the Defense Technical Information Center**, of which 969 are report primaries, being 15.9 percent, by the identifier rule set out under The Definition of Primary. 5,868 of the records carry a year, with a median of 2008, and 36.8 percent of those are from 2015 or later. **The programme's own documents are primaries by that rule** [Bell Aerospace Co Buffalo Ny 1953][research_bell_aerospace_co_buffalo_ny_1953] [Bell Aerospace Co Buffalo Ny 1954][research_bell_aerospace_co_buffalo_ny_1954] [Bell Aerospace Co Buffalo Ny 1956][research_bell_aerospace_co_buffalo_ny_1956], and so are the NACA rocket-model measurements of the configuration family [Moul and Wineman 1952][research_moul_1952] [Baber and Moul 1955][research_baber_1955].

The archival situation is the reverse of the [X-8][related_post_a305_aerojet_x8]'s and it is better.

A weapon programme reports to a service, and the service keeps the reports. The Defense Technical Information Center holds Bell's own project documents, reachable by digital object identifier under a single publisher prefix, and they cover the Shrike and the RASCAL together as the programme itself did. The aerospace archive holds something different and equally useful, which is the independent NACA measurement of the configuration family the X-9 belonged to.

**Neither archive holds much about the guidance system**, which is the vehicle's actual subject, and that is not an accident. Guidance was the classified part.

### The Definition of Primary

**Primacy is a property of the document, and this survey derives it from the identifier.** A record is a report primary when it is a NASA Technical Reports Server url or carries a digital object identifier under the 10.21236 prefix, which Crossref registers for Defense Technical Information Center reports. The Bell project documents, the NACA rocket-model and airborne-simulator reports and the period studies of guidance architectures and guidance response are reached that way, so the rule counts them. The period journal papers on which the estimator and tracking-error arguments rest, in the Journal of the American Statistical Association and the Proceedings of the Institute of Radio Engineers, are not.

**The rule does not reach the journal and conference literature of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, abbreviated AIAA.** 1,892 of the records carry its 10.2514 prefix, and among them are flight test and design papers written by the people who built the vehicles they describe. **15.9 percent is therefore a lower bound on how much of this survey is first-hand.**

### Thin Subjects

**Ten subjects that this article's derivations depend on have thin literatures.** Each count below is the number of research records in this survey whose title carries at least one of the listed terms, with a hyphen read as a space.

| Subject | Title terms counted | Records |
|---|---|---|
| the trapeze and the release mechanism | trapeze, displacement gear, release mechanism | 1 |
| the tip-off rate at release | tip off, tipoff | 1 |
| the data rate of the command link | data rate, bit rate | 1 |
| the crossover model of the human operator | crossover | 4 |
| the guidance time constant and the miss it leaves | time constant, guidance lag, autopilot lag | 8 |
| the division of thrust between two chambers | dual thrust, two chamber, twin chamber, dual chamber, multi chamber, sustainer, boost sustain | 7 |
| body bending against the autopilot | bending | 2 |
| the recovery temperature of the boundary layer | recovery temperature, recovery factor, adiabatic wall temperature | 0 |
| the transient temperature of a thin skin | skin temperature, transient temperature, thin skinned | 6 |
| the lethal radius | lethal radius, lethal area, lethal volume | 6 |

**The release is the thinnest subject of all, and what literature it has treats it as hardware.** The one record on a release mechanism is [Paradise 1971][research_paradise_1971], the one on tip-off is [Stippes 1962][research_stippes_1962], and no title names a trapeze, so the release-error and tip-off arithmetic in Sizing From First Principles stands on the relations shown there.

**The crossover model is thin because its vocabulary does not discriminate.** Four titles carry the word. Three name the model, [Jackson 1967][research_jackson_1967], [Jackson 1969][research_jackson_1969] and [Martinez-Garcia et al. 2017][research_martinezgarcia_gordon_2017], and one, [Smirnov 2019][research_smirnov_2019], uses it for the scattering of a radar target, while 92 titles in the human operator cluster describe manual control under other names. **The guidance time constant is thin in the same way.** Six of its eight records are modern guidance laws that compensate an autopilot lag, and the residual miss of a lagged loop is otherwise carried by the miss-distance titles of the guidance cluster.

**The data rate of the command link appears in one title**, [Kleider et al][research_kleider_gifford], and that title concerns an anti-jam waveform, which is consistent with this article's finding that capacity is not the difficulty of a command link. **Dividing thrust between two chambers is a solid-motor subject in these titles.** Three of its seven records name a single-chamber dual-thrust motor, [Hu et al. 1994][research_hu_zhang_1994], [Kwon 2020][research_kwon_2020] and [Yang et al. 2025a][research_yang_ji_2025], and two concern liquid engines with more than one chamber, [Tang et al. 2026][research_tang_huang_2026] and [Masyagin 2026][research_masyagin_2026], so the inference that the X-9's second chamber existed to match cruise drag stands on the drag arithmetic, as the Epistemic State records.

**Body bending against the autopilot has two records**, [Freed and Miller 1961][research_freed_1961] on damping bending modes for autopilot design and [Kawiecki and Smith 1994][research_kawiecki_smith_1994] on an actuator that avoids structural coupling. **The recovery temperature appears in no title, against 132 that name aerodynamic heating**, because it is a textbook relation, and the transient of a thin skin has six records, among them [Huston et al. 1948][research_huston_1948] and [Lo 1948][research_lo_1948], which the heating section relies on. **The lethal radius has six records**, and the scaling of blast with yield that the founding irony rests on is carried by [Morton 1966][research_morton_1966] and by the weapon-effects handbook the article cites.

### What the Survey Admits

**Every research title has been read for relevance, and a record is admitted only when a person reading its title finds it on this article's subject**, which is the accuracy of a command-guided, air-launched missile and everything the article dimensions to buy it, from the statistics of the circular error probable through the tracker, the operator, the guidance law, the autopilot, the airframe, the rocket and the launch, to the weapon effects that set the requirement and the successors that inherited the mission. The missile literature and the hypersonic glide literature are this article's subject and are admitted.

**Many words this subject depends on also name something else, and a record that shares only such a word is excluded.** Probable error is also a statistic of correlation coefficients, Mendelian ratios, astronomical parallaxes and water clocks, and single shot also names a film, a laser pulse and an object detector. Operator also names a mathematical operator and the crossover operator of a genetic algorithm, and the operators of ships, mines and nuclear control rooms are not the operator of a weapon. Line-of-sight guidance also steers ships, hovercraft and robots along a path, and a guided-missile destroyer is a ship. A slender body also moves through the internal waves of the ocean, an aerodynamic balance is also a force-measuring instrument, and the transient heating of skin is also a subject of thermal medicine. Air launch also delivers balloons, sondes, sonobuoys and ground-penetrating radars, radar beacons and monopulse also serve air traffic control, and the guidance of spacecraft, landers and planetary probes is a different problem. The geology, hydrology and weather of the missile ranges are not missile testing, and the policy, strategy and diplomacy of missile defence are not its engineering. Correction and retraction notices, encyclopedia volumes, journal issues and subject indexes are excluded as well, because a survey counts research works and those are editorial events or parts of works. A review of a book, a reference or definition entry, a notice such as front matter, an editorial or a news item, and a second deposit of a document already counted are not admitted either, since none of them is a research work in its own right.

**Some records of doubtful relevance are kept.** Robot and manipulator teleoperation across a communication delay is kept because closing a loop across a variable delay is the problem the review above names as the modern form of the X-9's link, and the allocation of functions between operators and automation in other vehicles is kept for the same operator-in-the-loop argument. Drift compensation for micro-machined and fibre-optic gyroscopes is kept as the instrument the autopilot section's drift argument concerns, reliability demonstration outside missiles is kept as the construct the flight test record uses, and the recovery parachutes of capsules, boosters, aircraft and airdrop are kept as recovery technique. The flight control of air-breathing hypersonic vehicles, the hinge moments of aircraft control surfaces, the multi-target tracking filters of radar networks and the combustion of solid rocket motors each share a method with this subject and are kept, as are four records the article cites for a neighbouring point, a flutter study of a piezoelectric plate, a fault-tolerance study for aeroengines, a latency study of remote driving and a study of silos under blast. A reader may weigh each accordingly.

**Because every title has been read, the off-topic share that remains is a matter of reading judgement.** The largest class removed is missile policy, because the word missile also names a subject of strategy, diplomacy and arms control.

## Epistemic State

**Historical fact, well documented.** The 15 July 1945 military characteristics and their 500 feet at 75 percent accuracy requirement. The MX-767 to MX-776 lineage and the MX-776A and MX-776B split. Bell's May 1947 development contract and Dornberger's leadership. The RTV-A-4 designation and its 1951 redesignation to X-9. The first glide drop in April 1949, the failed powered attempt in May 1950, the first full success on the fifth flight in November 1950, and the January 1953 conclusion. Thirty-one vehicles built. Trapeze launch from a modified EB-50D with radio command guidance. RASCAL cancellation in September 1958, which one directory gives as November.

**Engineering analysis, computed here.** The conversion of the accuracy requirement into an axis standard deviation of 91.5 metres and a circular error probable of 108 metres, the equal-share error budget, the radar cross-range resolution and the resulting launcher-guided range limit, the opposite error gradients of the two architectures, the operator crossover frequency, the airframe short-period frequency, the propellant load and burn time, the cruise-drag argument for two chambers, the air-launch energy credit, the glide ratio, the canard trim relations and the acceleration per degree, the release-error propagation, the separation time, the command link budget and data rate, the autopilot damping requirement, the recovery temperature and skin time constant, the canopy sizing, and the kill-probability inversion. **Each depends on assumed values stated where they are used.**

**Inference, stated as such.** That the launcher-guided range limit derived from a beamwidth explains the X-9's demonstrated range is a correspondence between two numbers and not a documented rationale, and the period sources compare guidance architectures on tactical grounds without ever performing this calculation. That the two-chamber engine existed to match cruise drag is inferred from the arithmetic and not from a source. That the trapeze exists to remove release-condition variance rather than merely to provide clearance is inferred the same way. That it lowered the X-9 clear of the bay before release is inferred from the mechanism, since the sources consulted say only that the vehicle was launched from a trapeze in the bomb bay.

**Not settled by the record consulted here.**

The number of X-9 flights, given as twenty-two in one account and twenty-eight in the NASA inventory, against thirty-one built.

The maximum speed, given as greater than Mach 1.5 by one compilation and Mach 2.0 by another.

The specific impulse and burn time of the XLR65-BA-1, neither of which was located, so the propulsion figures here are derived from masses and an assumed specific impulse.

Whether the X-9 ever demonstrated the accuracy the specification demanded. No source consulted states a measured circular error probable, which for a vehicle whose keystone is accuracy is a substantial gap.

The division of work between the two thrust chambers, and whether the second was shut down in cruise as the drag arithmetic suggests.

## Out of Scope

The GAM-63 RASCAL is treated only where it illuminates the X-9. Its development, its cancellation, and the air-launched ballistic missile programmes that displaced it are a larger subject.

The German V-1 air-launch experience and the JB-2 programme are context rather than subject.

The classified guidance hardware is not described because the accessible record does not describe it.

Sibling testbeds of the same era, including the Northrop MX-775 series, appear only by way of comparison.

## Conclusion

The X-9 is the first vehicle in this series whose keystone is a control loop and whose specification is a probability.

Reading that specification as a variance makes the design legible. One hundred and eight metres of circular error at a hundred miles, decomposed across subsystems in quadrature, is what dimensions the guidance link, the autopilot, the release mechanism, and the propulsion repeatability. It is also what forbids the obvious architecture, because a radar in the launch aircraft resolves an angle, and an angle at a hundred miles is a quarter of a kilometre. **Guiding from the launcher makes the error grow with the standoff that is the entire point of the weapon.** Guiding from the missile makes it shrink on approach. The weapon that resulted was named for its guidance link, and the name is the correct one.

The vehicle around that argument is unremarkable and is meant to be. A canard cruciform missile at Mach 2 needs no exotic material, its aerodynamics were being measured independently by NACA in the same years, and its rocket delivers more impulse than the airframe can use. What it needed was to fly the same way twice, and the record's shape, with eighteen months between the first drop and the first powered success and then a programme that stopped early because it was finished, is what a guidance programme looks like.

**The founding irony is that the requirement was written one day before Trinity.** Five hundred feet at seventy-five percent was specified before any nuclear weapon had been demonstrated, and the weapon that flew carried a warhead for which eight times that error would have sufficed. The accuracy work was mostly surplus to the mission and mostly useful to everything afterwards, which is a fair description of a great deal of research and is not a criticism.
